findings.title: Normalize email addresses before storing and matching blocklist entries
findings.body: The lookup uses case-sensitive equality, and BlockedEmail does not normalize addresses when storing them or checking them. An entry for `blocked@example.com` therefore does not match `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM`, although domain casing does not change the mailbox. The signup flow assigns the submitted email directly, allowing a blocked user to bypass this restriction by changing the domain's casing. Apply consistent email canonicalization to both stored entries and lookup values.

findings.title: Require a nonempty email-error array before rejecting an address
findings.body: EmailValidator reads `record.errors[:email]` even when the email passes validation, which creates an empty array in ActiveModel::Errors. The controller's `errors.to_hash` consequently includes `email: []` when signup fails for another field. Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript, so this condition caches the valid address as rejected—for example, after a username becomes unavailable between the availability check and submission. Correcting the username then leaves submission disabled until the email changes or the page reloads. Check that the email-error array contains an error before caching the address.

findings.title: Update match statistics atomically
findings.body: The method reads match_count, increments it in Ruby, and saves it without locking the row. Concurrent checks for the same address can both read the same count and overwrite each other with the same incremented value, losing matches. An older request can also overwrite a newer last_match_at value. Use an atomic database update or a row lock to preserve these statistics.

findings.title: Blocked-match statistics are rolled back by failed user saves
findings.body: Calling the mutating should_block? method during User validation makes its statistics update part of the surrounding User#save transaction. When the address is blocked, this validator adds an error and the user save rolls back, undoing BlockedEmail's match_count and last_match_at updates too. Paths that call save directly, such as User.create_for_email, therefore reject the address without recording the match. Persist match tracking outside the failing user-save transaction and cover a blocked User#save in an integration test.
